prospect.name: Douglas Rosa
prospect.occupation: Desk-based office work; joined the call from a work computer and a company Zoom account. Employer and job title not stated.
prospect.family_status: Married; lives with his wife and his mother-in-law. Two adult children, both married within four months of each other in the past year; first grandchild born February 2026 and a second due August 2026. Both children live nearby.
prospect.training_background: Five years of consistent gym training, four to five sessions a week at 5:30-6am. Two to three years of small-group HIIT classes at $300/month before switching in January 2026 to a cheaper gym with his wife. Roughly two months of self-directed kettlebell training copied from Trevor's Instagram, plus assisted pull-ups, push-ups and dumbbell chest press. Always starts with stretching and a foam roller. 7,000-10,000 steps a day. Played racquetball and occasional golf; not a sports person otherwise.
prospect.medical: Right shoulder injury that limits movement and fatigues faster on a straight overhead dumbbell press. Prior right patellar tendon injury, which he says now works better than his other knee. Flat feet, having lost about an inch of height. Hunched posture from desk work. His wife recently had a cancer scare that resolved with no radiation or chemotherapy required — the prospect himself disclosed no active condition.

signals: Self-directed and capable — has trained himself 4-5x/week for five years and taught himself kettlebells from free Instagram content.
The cheap alternative is genuinely working: 'I've seen my arms and everything, my change since I've been doing the kettlebells, which has been about two months.'
Left a $300/month gym explicitly on cost and moved to one at 'like a third of the price'.
Anchored hard on a number before hearing the offer: 'On the 2-3 range, that's what I was thinking.'
Not skeptical of the method or the coach — he believes both work; the resistance is entirely price-to-substitute.

goals.text: Break the plateau and get from 209 lb down toward 190 lb
Lose the spare tire around his waist and feel better about how he looks and feels — self-esteem
Get in shape now at 59 rather than leaving it too late, and keep mobility as he ages
Stay healthy and physically able to play with his grandchildren, who are arriving in quick succession
Get a structured programme instead of piecing it together from videos — 'just haven't been able to figure out the formula'

pains.text: Weighs 209 lb every single day for two years and cannot move it despite training four to five times a week
Sweet tooth and eating after 8pm; describes it as a bad habit he keeps repeating
Lost the external obligation that used to keep him consistent when he was paying for booked group sessions
Training himself off online videos with no coaching — 'I've had no real training'
Hunched posture from sitting at a desk all day, and a right shoulder that fatigues faster on overhead pressing

objections.raw_quote: Well, listen, Andrew, I'm getting honest with you. That's way more than I thought it was going to be. So I'm going to have to say, I'm out.
objections.rep_response: Isolated the money — asked whether, money aside, he would actually want to do it — then said he was trying to find a way to make the investment 'more digestible'.

objections.raw_quote: I can continue to educate myself online, but I can't invest that much.
objections.rep_response: Did not run the scripted financial picture (cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, investments). Went straight to restructuring the offer.

objections.raw_quote: Well, me tell you this. Let me think about it and see how I can possibly work that number. If I'm allowed, then I'll reach back out to you.
objections.rep_response: Did not run the think-about-it play. Restated the six-month guarantee and then invented a three-month option at $4,000 with a possible top-up to six months.

objections.raw_quote: I'll take the items you gave me today to heart. I'll try to implement some of that myself. And I'll keep using Trevor's videos.
objections.rep_response: Reframed information versus structure — 'everything is out there... but the thing is, the structure, the program, that's the essence' — then introduced third-party financing and emailed a Klarna option.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep offered to 'break it in half with no interest' and then emailed a third-party financing option (Klarna) that could spread payments up to 12 months. No amounts, dates or instalment schedule were agreed.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Because the six months is the full transformation, yeah? And that comes with a guarantee also. Because six months is the period that Trevor needs to work with someone so he can guarantee the result. If you want to get the result that adding those extra weight on kettlebells and so on, he will work with you for free for next months.

evidence: Explicit refusal after the financing email arrived: 'Okay, I got it. No, I'm not going to do it. Sorry, Andrew.'
First refusal at price reveal: 'That's way more than I thought it was going to be. So I'm going to have to say, I'm out.'
Second refusal to the discounted three-month tier: 'No, I think it's not going to work. It's just a little too pricey for my liking.'

Counter-evidence: mid-objection he did say 'Let me think about it and see how I can possibly work that number... then I'll reach back out to you', and the rep closed with 'If you feel like in the future just that you're capable, just reach out to us' — so the relationship is not burned, but the answer on this call was a clear no.
Counter-evidence: the prospect's belief in the method was never the blocker — 'It's not like I don't believe it.'
outcome.next_step: None booked. Prospect said he would implement the advice himself and keep following Trevor's free videos; rep left an open invitation to come back if his finances change.

notable.note: Three separate pricing structures were put in front of the prospect after he declined: a three-month tier at $4,000 that does not exist in the stated offer, an interest-free split into two payments, and third-party consumer credit via Klarna sent by email. The rep also stated the guarantee is contingent on six months and then offered the three-month tier without addressing what happens to the guarantee. Discovery was strong on baseline facts but the consequence frame was never run at all, so the price landed with no cost-of-inaction behind it. The anchor that killed the deal is the company's own free Instagram content, which the prospect says is already working for him.
